sections.html:
Taylorsville is in the middle of the Salt Lake Valley in Salt Lake County, and it is part of the Salt Lake City metropolitan area. The city covers 10.85 square miles, all land, at an elevation of about 4,295 feet.

Interstate 215 and Bangerter Highway run beside it, and Redwood Road is another major road through town. The ground is a flat alluvial plain left by Lake Bonneville. An inactive fault, the Taylorsville Fault, crosses the valley, and Bennion Hill, a ridge about 150 feet above the surrounding area, rises to the east.

The 2020 census counted 21,371 housing units and 20,615 households in the city, with a median age of 34.7. The area grew fast before it was a city: its population rose from 17,448 in 1980 to 52,354 in 1990, so a large share of the houses date from those years.

sections.h2: How did Taylorsville begin, and when did it become a city?
sections.html:
Taylorsville was settled in 1848, when Joseph and Susanna Harker built a log cabin in November of that year. Early names included Harker's Settlement and Field's Bottom, the first successful crop came in 1851, and the English Fort went up in 1854. The area had 178 residents in 1860.

Farming shaped the area for a century. Local crops included corn, wheat, oats, alfalfa and sugar beets, and the West Jordan Sugar Factory opened in 1916. In the 1980s the Redwood Road and 5400 South intersection became a regional shopping center.

Voters approved incorporation in September 1995 with more than 70% in favor, and Taylorsville became a city on July 1, 1996. It was formed from the Taylorsville-Bennion area and parts of the Kearns metro township. Camp Kearns, opened in 1942 to the west, is outside the city limits. The city runs its own police and code enforcement, while fire service comes through the Unified Fire Authority.

sections.h2: Taylorsville at a glance: what do the Census numbers show?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts the median owner-occupied home value in Taylorsville at $433,800 for 2020 to 2024. The city is dense, at about 5,572 people per square mile in 2020.

The 2025 estimate is below the 2020 count, which is unusual for the Wasatch Front and worth knowing if you are guessing how many buyers are in the area.

Taylorsville's economy moved from farming to retail. The sugar beet and grain fields gave way to shopping along Redwood Road and 5400 South, where Harmons and Walmart are among the businesses.

  • Salt Lake Community College's Redwood campus is in Taylorsville.
  • The city runs its own court, and Taylorsville Court established the second DUI court in the nation.
  • The city has a mayor, Kristie Overson, and a five-member council elected by district.

No single employer dominates the city, so a Taylorsville house is rarely tied to the fortunes of one company. Shopping, the college and the freeways are the draws buyers mention.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and transit serve Taylorsville?
sections.html:
Taylorsville is in the Granite School District, which was formed in 1904 when the Salt Lake County Commission combined 22 of 36 local districts. Schools named in the city's history include Plymouth Elementary and Kearns Junior High, and Madison School began in 1894 as the 64 District School.

Transit has a long history here. The Salt Lake Inter-Urban line ran beside Redwood Road starting in 1913, and the Bingham-Garfield Railroad crossed the area in 1910. Bennion became its own church ward in 1905.

The main roads today are Interstate 215, Bangerter Highway, Redwood Road and 2700 West, once called Pole Line Road, which was built in 1927. A planned bus line, the Midvalley Connector, would link Murray Central TRAX and FrontRunner station with the SLCC Redwood campus and West Valley Central. Along 4700 South in Taylorsville, buses would use dedicated center lanes between about Atherton Drive and Redwood Road.

The project page we reviewed showed the line in environmental review with no opening date, so treat it as a plan. Check the Utah Transit Authority for the current status.

sections.h2: Which Taylorsville city rules affect owners and landlords?
sections.html:
Taylorsville enforces its city codes and zoning ordinances through its own code enforcement office. Most issues are resolved quickly once the owner is contacted, and owners who will not comply can face legal action to abate the nuisance.

  • Code enforcement phone numbers: 801-955-2013 and 801-955-2053. Complaints can also be filed online.
  • The city stopped issuing Good Landlord Program licenses after June 30, 2023, and rental business licenses are being combined into a single category.
  • A house with open code violations is easier to sell once they are cleared, so ask for a status check before listing.

If you are a landlord selling a rented house, check that your business license is current and confirm with the city what applies to a buyer who keeps it as a rental.

sections.h2: What are the Salt Lake County tax dates for a Taylorsville seller?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County property taxes are due November 30, and the county Auditor mails valuation notices on July 22. Official tax notices must go out by November 1.

DateWhat happens

August 1Board of Equalization opens for appeals, for 45 days
September 15Appeals close, or 45 days after the notice, whichever is later
November 1Tax notices must be mailed
November 30Last day to pay without a penalty
December 1Unpaid taxes are delinquent; penalty is the greater of 2.5% or $10
January 31Penalty drops to the greater of 1% or $10 if all is paid
Fourth Thursday of MayTraditional date of the final tax sale

Source: Salt Lake County Treasurer dates and deadlines. Properties stay redeemable until March 15 of the fifth year after delinquency. Utah exempts 45% of a primary residence's value, up to one acre, and your title company prorates the current bill at closing.

sections.h2: What do Taylorsville sellers usually deal with?
sections.html:
Many Taylorsville houses date from the growth years of the 1980s and 1990s. Houses of that age can need a new roof, sewer line, windows or electrical panel, and an owner may not want to fund that before selling.

The other common situations are rentals with a difficult tenant, an estate with several heirs, a house with code citations and a move that cannot wait. In those cases an as-is offer removes the repair list, the showings and the commission.

We buy houses in Taylorsville as-is, and you choose whether to accept the offer.

faqs.q: When are Taylorsville property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30. Taylorsville is in Salt Lake County, where unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1 with a penalty of 2.5% or $10, whichever is greater.

faqs.q: How do I report a code violation in Taylorsville?
faqs.a: Call Taylorsville code enforcement at 801-955-2013 or 801-955-2053, or file a complaint online through the city's code enforcement page.

Taylorsville has a mayor and a five-member city council elected by district, with nonpartisan elections. The city has its own police and code enforcement, and fire service comes through the Unified Fire Authority, where the city holds a board seat.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Taylorsville rental with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses with tenants in place and as-is. Tell us the lease terms and rent so we can give you a clear offer.
